reasoning: The December 2013 meeting marks the initiation of QE tapering — a concrete operational change from $85B/month to $75B/month in asset purchases beginning January 2014 — which constitutes the introduction of a new trajectory (from steady accommodation to gradual withdrawal of QE). This is precisely the type of program-termination onset that qualifies as a major pivot, analogous to the 2021-11 taper announcement. The prior October meeting explicitly held purchases steady awaiting 'more evidence,' while December acted on cumulative progress. Additionally, the forward guidance was strengthened to offset the taper signal, with the Committee adding that it 'likely will be appropriate to maintain the current target range for the federal funds rate well past the time that the unemployment rate declines below 6-1/2 percent,' a material change to the rate threshold framework.
key_quote: In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions, the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases. Beginning in January, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $40 billion per month rather than $45 billion per month.
